data.name: Rocket Armor
data.detailed_description:
Rocket Armor is the most realistic and exciting flying experience in VR today! It features a completely new type of flight control system and maneuvering capability – it’s like really flying using two huge rockets strapped to your arms! Rocket Armor suits you up in a suit of futuristic armor and sets you on a timed course through space, hitting platform marks and maneuvering through ring structures in ever more complex patterns while fighting off alien enemies with your laser and sword weapons. You fly with true freedom of movement and a full range of motion in space – all controlled by your powerful arm-mounted rockets. Feel the thundering acceleration as you shoot upward and then plunge back to earth, or power into a sharp turn at full throttle.

You learn the skills needed to fly the Rocket Armor and qualify as an Alpha Pilot. Fight and fly to complete all the levels and be prepared for more difficult and dangerous missions in the future. This is the ultimate free flight experience in VR (and a fantastic game)! So SUIT UP Alpha Pilot and join us for the Rocket Armor ride!










Key Features

• Realistic rocket powered free flight (using hand controllers), designed and engineered specifically for VR – controlled speed, full maneuverability

• Dynamic gameplay with multiple, increasingly difficult levels over constantly changing terrain indoors and outdoors

• Fly through obstacles and touching down on platforms over a timed course, fighting off enemies that can disrupt your flight path

• Laser and sword weapons enable fast-paced 3D combat with swarm AI enemy

• Offline leaderboard tracking allows you to see your competitive position based on your time over the course

• Original, dramatic soundtrack works to increase the pilot’s sense of immersion and excitement

• Alpha Pilot certification is earned on completion of the 10 levels, qualifying the pilot for future Rocket Armor missions and adventures which are currently in development

reviews.review:
Rocket Armor is a small VR flight game that caught my attention because the entire idea is built around flying with rockets attached to my arms. Instead of sitting inside a normal aircraft, I am wearing futuristic armour and using my motion controllers to move through the air. The game puts me through timed courses where I have to fly through rings, reach platforms and deal with alien enemies along the way. It is a very specific idea, but I think that makes it more interesting than trying to be another normal flight simulator.

The flying is easily the best part for me. Having control over my movement through my hands gives the game a much more physical feeling than a traditional flight game. I can accelerate, turn and move around freely, and there is something satisfying about getting a difficult section right after initially struggling with the controls. The courses gradually introduce more complicated patterns, so I have to get better at controlling the rockets rather than simply relying on a normal forward flying system.

There is combat as well, which gives me something else to think about while I am flying. I have a laser and a sword that I can use against alien enemies, and some enemies can interfere with my flight path. I like the combination because I am not just following a course and trying to beat a time. I have to keep control of my movement while also dealing with enemies around me. The combat is fairly simple, but it works as an extra layer on top of the flying instead of taking over the whole game.

The biggest problem for me is the amount of content. Rocket Armor has 10 courses and is built around completing them as quickly as possible, with offline leaderboards recording my times. That gives me a reason to replay the courses and try to improve, but there is not a huge amount of variety beyond mastering what is already there. Once I understand the flight system and have completed the courses, I am mostly playing for better times. That can be fun for a while, but I do not think the game has enough depth to keep me interested for a really long time.

I also have to judge the game as what it actually is today rather than what it originally promised to become. Development was discontinued and the game was made completely free, with the current version described by the developer as a complete playable experience. That is good because I can try the whole thing without paying anything, but it also means there are no future missions or larger adventures coming to expand the concept. The game works as a compact time attack experience, but I can definitely see the potential for something much bigger that was never made.

The presentation is decent for a small VR project from 2017. The futuristic armour, alien enemies and changing environments give me enough to look at while I am flying, and the original soundtrack helps make the courses feel more exciting. It is not a game I would play for its story because there really is not much of one. The main appeal is the feeling of controlling myself in three dimensional space, and I think the game understands that. It is also worth remembering that this is VR only, so it has a very specific audience and cannot really be treated like a normal PC flight game.

Overall, Rocket Armor is a fun little experiment that gets its main idea right. I like the unusual arm controlled flight, the timed courses, the combination of flying and combat and the satisfaction of learning how to move properly through the levels. The 10 course structure and lack of further development limit the amount of content, and the simple combat means the flying is doing most of the work. Still, because it is completely free and focuses on a genuinely different way of moving through VR, I think it is worth trying if I already have the equipment for it. It is not a huge game, but what is here is enjoyable enough to make the concept worthwhile.

Rating: 7.3/10
